overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals that astronomical and planetary 'What If' scenarios and extreme space phenomena generate the highest views-per-day, likes-per-view, and comment engagement. Specifically, immersive second-person hypothetical hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with extreme planetary anomalies (diamonds, dark planets, extreme weather) significantly outperform abstract science or standard historical/psychological facts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) show exceptionally high engagement ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more high-concept 'What If' scenarios placing the viewer directly into extreme cosmic environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring bizarre physical realities like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views), 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views), and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,031 views) drive superior algorithmic velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Focus future scripts on bizarre, counter-intuitive planetary physics and extreme space weather.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on internal human psychology or memory tricks (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', views as low as 5 to 53) demonstrate poor momentum and low like-to-view ratios.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological trivia in favor of high-visual-potential space and physics concepts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts covering standard biological facts without a high-stakes cinematic hook (e.g., standard animal lifespan or basic trivia) underperform compared to cosmic extremes.
weak_patterns.action: Elevate biological and historical concepts by framing them around existential paradoxes or cinematic survival narratives.
